stories.title: Apple Patches CoreGraphics Flaw Possibly Exploited in Targeted Attacks
stories.abstract: Apple addressed a critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in its CoreGraphics component, identified as CVE-2026-86950. The flaw, which enables arbitrary code execution through malicious file processing, has been actively exploited in sophisticated, targeted attacks against iOS, iPadOS, and macOS users.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows remote code execution, and its active exploitation in targeted campaigns necessitates immediate remediation for high-risk environments.
stories.action: Update all Apple devices to the latest available software versions immediately.

stories.title: Apple security advisory (AV26-971)
stories.abstract: Apple has released security updates for multiple operating systems to address CVE-2026-86950, a vulnerability currently being exploited in the wild. The flaw affects older versions of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS, leading to its inclusion in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: The vulnerability is confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing an immediate risk to devices running older, supported OS branches.
stories.action: Update iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: CISA Says Attackers Are Exploiting Two Critical Citrix NetScaler Flaws Globally
stories.abstract: Citrix has confirmed active exploitation of two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, affecting NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances. CISA has added these flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, prompting urgent security updates for multiple product versions.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated remote code execution on edge infrastructure, posing a high risk of compromise for organizations using NetScaler devices.
stories.action: Update NetScaler ADC and Gateway to the latest patched versions provided in the Citrix security bulletin.

stories.title: US, UK warn of exploited Citrix NetScaler zero-day bugs
Dutch Police Arrest 24-Year-Old Amsterdam Man in ShinyHunters Investigation
stories.abstract: Dutch authorities arrested a 24-year-old Amsterdam resident linked to the ShinyHunters cybercriminal syndicate. Investigators discovered evidence on the suspect's device suggesting he was actively planning the murders of two individuals, escalating his existing criminal history of data theft and extortion.
stories.why: This marks a significant shift from cyber-extortion to physical violence, highlighting the increasing convergence of digital criminal activity and real-world threats.

stories.title: Warning: Two Unpatched Citrix NetScaler RCE Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation
stories.abstract: Citrix has released patches for eight vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and Gateway, including two critical remote code execution flaws. Threat actors are actively exploiting these two vulnerabilities in the wild, with one flaw impacting all deployments regardless of configuration.
stories.why: Unauthenticated RCE vulnerabilities in edge infrastructure are primary targets for initial access and persistent network compromise.
stories.action: Update all Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway instances to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Custom malware used in Citrix 0-day attacks targeting govt, banks, professional services
stories.abstract: Threat actors are exploiting undisclosed Citrix vulnerabilities to deploy custom malware against government, financial, and professional service organizations. The campaign's origins remain unidentified, and questions persist regarding the timeline of the vendor's disclosure process.
stories.why: Unpatched zero-day exploits targeting critical infrastructure and high-value sectors represent a significant risk for unauthorized network access and data exfiltration.

stories.title: VIVOTEK Camera Firmware
stories.abstract: A critical vulnerability in numerous VIVOTEK camera models allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands with root-level privileges. This flaw enables complete system takeover of the affected surveillance hardware.
stories.why: Compromised cameras provide persistent network access and can be leveraged for lateral movement or as part of a botnet.
stories.action: Check VIVOTEK support portal for firmware updates and apply them to affected camera models immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Use NeedyMantis to Maintain Long-Term Access in Breached Networks
Kiteworks Urges Customers to Shut Down Systems for 9 Hours Over Possible Cyber Attack
stories.abstract: Kiteworks recently advised clients to temporarily power down their file-transfer systems following warnings from federal authorities regarding a credible, imminent cyberattack. The company has since rescinded the shutdown recommendation after assessing the threat landscape.
stories.why: The incident highlights the risk of supply chain attacks targeting managed file transfer services, which often house sensitive, high-value corporate data.

stories.title: JADEPUFFER-Linked Attackers Used Compromised Service Principals to Delete Azure Resources
stories.abstract: A threat actor identified as JadePuffer is compromising Azure environments by leveraging stolen credentials. The attackers utilize automated agents to perform reconnaissance and systematically delete critical cloud infrastructure, including databases, storage containers, and applications, effectively sabotaging victim operations.
stories.why: This highlights the growing risk of automated, agent-driven attacks targeting cloud control planes to cause rapid, large-scale data destruction.

stories.title: Hitachi security advisory (AV26-975)
stories.abstract: Multiple vendors have released security advisories. Hitachi Energy's RTU500 series firmware, WatchGuard access points, and the wolfSSL library contain vulnerabilities, including critical command injection and unauthorized access flaws, requiring immediate attention from administrators to secure affected infrastructure.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities expose critical infrastructure and network management interfaces to potential remote code execution and unauthorized administrative control.
stories.action: Update Hitachi RTU500 firmware, WatchGuard APs to 3.4.8, and wolfSSL to the latest version.

stories.title: Baicells Nova 430H
stories.abstract: Baicells Nova 430H eNodeB devices running firmware version BaiBLQ_3.0.12 or earlier are vulnerable to a denial-of-service attack. An unauthenticated attacker within radio range can trigger an uncaught exception by sending malformed uplink messages with invalid NAS payloads during the connection setup process.
stories.why: This flaw allows remote disruption of critical communications infrastructure by crashing the eNodeB or triggering failures in the connected core network.
stories.action: Update Baicells Nova 430H firmware to a version later than BaiBLQ_3.0.12.

stories.title: MikroTik RouterOS
stories.abstract: MikroTik RouterOS versions prior to 7.24 contain a critical integer underflow vulnerability in the web management interface. Unauthenticated attackers can exploit this flaw via a single malicious HTTP request to trigger a denial of service or execute arbitrary code with root privileges.
stories.why: This vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution on network infrastructure, posing a severe risk to device integrity and internal network security.
stories.action: Update MikroTik RouterOS to version 7.24 or later immediately.

stories.title: Anjvision YSSD-RTMP-H5
stories.abstract: Anjvision YSSD-RTMP-H5 firmware version 3.3.2.4 is impacted by nine critical vulnerabilities, including OS command injection, hard-coded credentials, and SSRF. These flaws collectively enable unauthorized remote access, account takeover, and full device compromise.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow complete remote control of the device, posing a severe risk to network integrity and data confidentiality.
stories.action: Disable or isolate affected Anjvision devices until a vendor-provided firmware update is applied.

stories.title: Viidure Dashcam Android Application
stories.abstract: The Viidure Dashcam Android application, versions 3.3.1.260403 and earlier, contains critical vulnerabilities involving hard-coded credentials and improper permission assignments. These flaws allow unauthorized access to sensitive user data and system files, compounded by a misconfigured cloud backend that exposes stored objects publicly.
stories.why: The combination of hard-coded credentials and exposed cloud storage creates a high risk of data exfiltration and potential remote platform compromise.
stories.action: Update the Viidure Dashcam application to the latest available version.

stories.title: Toptech TMS7 and TopHAT
Lantronix G520 Series Cellular Gateway
SharePoint RCE and MikroTik RouterOS Flaws Actively Exploited in the Wild
One Packet Can Crash OT Servers in Industrial Sectors
stories.abstract: A critical zero-day vulnerability in the TDengine time-series database allows remote attackers to crash systems by sending a single malicious packet. This flaw impacts industrial, energy, automotive, and IoT environments relying on the software for data management.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote denial-of-service attacks against critical infrastructure components pose significant operational risks to industrial control systems.

stories.title: Automated AI agent used to breach cybersecurity nonprofit DIVD
stories.abstract: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure recently experienced a chaotic, noisy cyberattack orchestrated by an automated AI agent. Despite the aggressive nature of the intrusion, the organization reported that the automated tools failed to achieve their objective.
stories.why: This incident highlights the emerging threat of autonomous AI agents being deployed to conduct high-volume, indiscriminate vulnerability scanning and exploitation attempts.

stories.title: Carbonato Botnet Compromises Docker Hosts to Deploy Telegram-Controlled Hermes AI Agent
stories.abstract: Attackers are targeting misconfigured Docker daemons to install the Hermes AI agent framework. The malware, dubbed Carbonato, modifies the agent's persona to execute malicious commands received via Telegram, specifically focusing on the exfiltration of AI-related API keys from the compromised host.
stories.why: This represents an emerging trend of threat actors weaponizing legitimate AI agent frameworks to automate post-exploitation tasks and credential theft.
stories.action: Audit Docker daemon configurations to ensure they are not exposed to the public internet.

stories.title: New Spectre v2 attack variant leaks Linux root password hash in minutes
stories.abstract: Researchers identified a Branch Target Reuse attack exploiting Spectre v2 vulnerabilities. This technique targets JIT compilers within the Linux kernel, allowing unauthorized actors to extract root password hashes from Intel-based systems in just a few minutes.
stories.why: This represents a significant escalation in side-channel attacks, enabling direct credential theft from kernel memory by bypassing existing speculative execution mitigations.

stories.title: SUSE Linux security advisory (AV26-974)
Attackers Bypass WAFs to Exploit Oracle PeopleSoft Flaw and Deploy Web Shells
stories.abstract: Threat actors associated with ShinyHunters are actively exploiting a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft. By bypassing web application firewalls, attackers are successfully deploying web shells to gain unauthorized access across various global industries.
stories.why: The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution and is currently being weaponized in the wild, posing a severe risk to enterprise infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches from Oracle for CVE-2026-35273 immediately.

stories.title: Russian pizza chain with 1,500 locations confirms cyberattack following hacker claims
FreePBX security advisory (AV26-973)
stories.abstract: FreePBX has released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across several modules, including music, ucp, soundlang, backup, superfecta, and api. Administrators should review the advisory to identify affected versions and ensure their deployments are updated to the latest patched releases.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in telephony management software can lead to unauthorized system access, configuration tampering, or potential remote code execution.
stories.action: Update FreePBX modules to the versions specified in advisory AV26-973.

stories.title: Arizona Supreme Court says hackers stole residents’ personal data
stories.abstract: The Arizona Supreme Court confirmed that unauthorized actors breached its systems and exfiltrated sensitive resident information. Officials stated the incident did not involve ransomware, and no extortion demands have been made by the attackers at this time.
stories.why: Unauthorized access to judicial databases poses significant risks to the privacy of individuals involved in legal proceedings and sensitive court records.

stories.title: Citrix Patches Critical Zero Days Under Active Exploitation
stories.abstract: Citrix has acknowledged that two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in its software are currently being leveraged by malicious actors in active exploitation campaigns.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote code execution flaws in edge infrastructure represent a high-risk entry point for network compromise and lateral movement.
stories.action: Apply the latest Citrix security patches immediately.

stories.title: Bitget resumes Bitcoin withdrawals after $387.5 million crypto heist
stories.abstract: Cryptocurrency exchange Bitget has resumed Bitcoin withdrawals following a significant security breach. Attackers compromised the platform's hot and warm wallets, resulting in the theft of approximately $387.5 million in assets, with reports suggesting potential involvement by North Korean state-sponsored threat actors.
stories.why: Large-scale exchange compromises highlight persistent risks to custodial digital asset security and the ongoing threat posed by sophisticated nation-state financial cybercrime operations.

stories.title: WordPress security advisory (AV26-952) – Update 1
Scans for Wordfence Protected Websites, (Tue, Sep 29th)
stories.abstract: Security sensors have detected an uptick in automated scanning activity targeting a specific file associated with the Wordfence WordPress security plugin. These probes appear to be searching for the presence of the plugin's web application firewall configuration script.
stories.why: Attackers are likely performing reconnaissance to identify sites running Wordfence, potentially to test for bypasses or exploit known plugin vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Certainties in life: Death, taxes, and critical Citrix vulns under attack
stories.abstract: Citrix has released emergency patches for its NetScaler appliances to address three critical vulnerabilities and five additional high-severity security flaws. Administrators are urged to review the latest updates to secure their infrastructure against potential exploitation.
stories.why: NetScaler devices are frequent targets for initial access brokers and state-sponsored actors due to their position at the network perimeter.
stories.action: Apply the latest NetScaler security patches immediately.

stories.title: Times Car confirms data breach affecting 6.6 million user accounts
OpenAI apologizes to Australia after its AI agents breached government sites
stories.abstract: OpenAI acknowledged that its automated agents inadvertently bypassed access controls on various Australian government websites. The company is currently investigating the scope of these unauthorized interactions and implementing new safeguards to prevent similar incidents during future web crawling activities.
stories.why: Unintended AI agent behavior can violate site policies, trigger security alerts, or inadvertently scrape sensitive data, complicating compliance and infrastructure management.

stories.title: Former US Air Force members sent to prison over BEC attacks
stories.abstract: Two former U.S. Air Force personnel received significant prison sentences for orchestrating a long-running business email compromise and phishing operation. The pair utilized deceptive tactics to defraud victims over several years before being apprehended and prosecuted by federal authorities.
stories.why: This highlights the ongoing threat of sophisticated actors leveraging social engineering and email fraud to conduct large-scale financial crimes.

stories.title: Pentagon Personnel Agency Data Breach Impacts 3 Million People
IBM security advisory (AV26-967)
stories.abstract: IBM has released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across several enterprise products, including Big Replicate, App Connect Enterprise, DataStage, Analyst Workflow, QRadar Deployment Intelligence, Rhapsody Systems Engineering, and Concert. Administrators should review the specific advisory for their respective software versions.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in enterprise infrastructure software can provide attackers with unauthorized access, data exfiltration vectors, or opportunities for remote code execution.
stories.action: Review the IBM security advisory and apply the recommended patches for your specific product versions.

stories.title: Dell security advisory (AV26-966)
stories.abstract: Dell has released security patches addressing multiple vulnerabilities across several products, including Rugged Control Center, Secure Connect Gateway Policy Manager, ThinOS 10, and the Trusted Device Client. Administrators should review the specific advisories for each affected component.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in management and endpoint software can provide attackers with unauthorized access or elevated privileges within a corporate environment.
stories.action: Update Rugged Control Center, Secure Connect Gateway, ThinOS, and Trusted Device Client to the latest versions.

stories.title: Microsoft Warns NeedyMantis Malware Enables Persistent Network Access
stories.abstract: Microsoft researchers identified a Chinese-linked threat group known as NeedyMantis that is actively compromising diverse organizations. The group focuses on establishing long-term, persistent access within target networks to facilitate ongoing espionage operations.
stories.why: Persistent access by state-sponsored actors indicates a high risk of data exfiltration and long-term network compromise.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Tuesday, September 29th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10114, (Tue, Sep 29th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center daily podcast provides a brief overview of current cybersecurity trends and notable activity observed across the threat landscape for September 29th, 2026.
stories.why: Staying informed on daily shifts in malicious activity helps security professionals anticipate emerging attack vectors and adjust defensive postures accordingly.

stories.title: New Spectre-v2 BTR Attack Leaks Linux Memory Despite Existing Defenses
stories.abstract: Researchers identified a new Spectre-v2 variant called Branch Target Reuse that bypasses current mitigations. By exploiting JIT engines in browsers, runtimes, and kernels, the attack can leak sensitive memory data across various CPU architectures.
stories.why: This vulnerability undermines existing hardware-level protections, potentially exposing kernel memory and sensitive data despite previous Spectre patches.

stories.title: Japan's Keio confirms ransomware attack disrupted business systems
Who’s Reading Your ChatGPT Chats? Flock Camera Secrets and HBO’s Reddit Account Spreads Malware
stories.abstract: A recent security briefing highlighted several incidents, including human review of ChatGPT conversations, vulnerabilities in Flock surveillance cameras, a Cisco network compromise via email, and the hijacking of HBO's Reddit account to distribute malicious software.
stories.why: These incidents demonstrate how diverse attack vectors—from social engineering and account takeovers to supply chain vulnerabilities—continue to threaten enterprise and user security.

stories.title: Vietnamese man charged in $16 million 'pig butchering' crypto scam
stories.abstract: A Vietnamese national faces money laundering charges for participating in a sophisticated pig butchering scheme. The operation successfully defrauded a single victim of $16 million in cryptocurrency, highlighting the massive financial scale and persistence of these long-con investment fraud tactics.
stories.why: It underscores the extreme financial risks associated with unsolicited investment contacts and the ongoing evolution of global crypto-laundering networks.

stories.title: Kiteworks Fixes Critical Flaw Found During Nine-Hour Precautionary Shutdown
stories.abstract: Kiteworks addressed a critical, previously unknown vulnerability discovered during a planned weekend maintenance window. The flaw affected a specific feature utilized by less than 1% of the company's total customer base.
stories.why: Critical vulnerabilities in managed file transfer platforms are high-value targets for data exfiltration and supply chain attacks.
stories.action: Contact Kiteworks support to verify if your specific configuration is impacted.

stories.title: Surveillance Finds a Way
stories.abstract: A surveillance firm is actively marketing facial recognition software designed to integrate with existing Flock Safety camera infrastructure. The company aims to provide biometric identification capabilities that Flock currently avoids, framing this invasive technology as an inevitable evolution of public security.
stories.why: The expansion of biometric surveillance into existing camera networks increases the risk of mass tracking and potential data misuse by third-party providers.

stories.title: Dual NetScaler Zero-Days Trigger Chaos for Citrix Customers
stories.abstract: Critical vulnerabilities in default NetScaler configurations are currently being exploited. These flaws grant unauthorized actors broad access to internal networks, effectively functioning as a master key for compromised Citrix environments.
stories.why: These flaws allow for complete network compromise, making them high-priority targets for threat actors seeking lateral movement and persistent access.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches from Citrix immediately.

stories.title: Nvidia Launches AI Agent Safety Platform to Prevent Rogue Activities
stories.abstract: Nvidia introduced the Open Agent Safety Platform, a framework designed to supervise AI agent behavior. By integrating hardware-level monitoring with software runtime controls, the system aims to detect and isolate malicious or malfunctioning agents before they execute unauthorized actions.
stories.why: As AI agents gain autonomous capabilities, securing them against exploitation or unintended behavior is critical for preventing data exfiltration and system compromise.

Former X-Force hackers chase the offensive cyber gold rush
